concepts.def: Deliberately ambiguous language used to mislead
Forces beyond natural law — witches, ghosts, visions
Jacobean idea of God-ordained social hierarchy
Influencing someone to act against their own will
A character whose contrast highlights another
Solo speech revealing a character's private thoughts

walkthroughs.body_html:
Lady Macbeth attacks her husband's masculinity: 'When you durst do it, then you were a man.'

She also invokes the supernatural: 'unsex me here, and fill me from the crown to the toe top-full of direst cruelty.' She wills herself out of her gender to commit regicide.

The witches deal in equivocation — truth that misleads.

'None of woman born shall harm Macbeth' is technically true (Macduff was 'untimely ripp'd' by C-section), but Macbeth hears it as immortality. Their language traps him.

After Duncan's murder, horses eat each other and an owl kills a falcon.

Jacobeans believed the king embodied natural order. Killing him fractures the cosmos — Shakespeare flatters his patron, James I, who survived an assassination attempt in 1605.

mcqs.q: What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to do in her famous soliloquy?
Why is Macduff able to kill Macbeth despite the prophecy?
options: He was born by Caesarean section
He is in fact a woman

numericals.q: In what year did the Gunpowder Plot fail — the event closest to Macbeth's writing?
numericals.hint: Macbeth was written around 1606, just after.

free_texts.q: What word means deliberately ambiguous language used to mislead? One word.
free_texts.hint: The witches deal in it constantly.
